life.name: Life events — what happens to you

rows.a: Aso-ebi and a wedding you cannot skip
rows.b: Your university friend is getting married. The aso-ebi alone is priced like a small appliance, and everyone will notice whether you showed up properly.

rows.a: Your father's blood pressure is not a joke
rows.b: The clinic in the village says he needs to see a specialist in the city. The tests are not free and neither is the trip.
A recruiter abroad has been pursuing you for months. The offer is real: a role, a relocation package, and a salary denominated in something that does not lose value while you sleep.

rows.a: A friend wants you into a round
rows.b: He has a deck, a prototype, and a deadline. He needs ₦500,000 and he is offering 4% of the company. He is also the third friend this year to ask.

rows.a: A man with a very confident smile
rows.b: He explains a structure. Import something, sell it, double your money in ninety days. He uses the word "guaranteed" four times in two minutes.
You have known them for two years. It is time to decide whether this becomes a formal thing with a ceremony, a family meeting, and a joint budget.

rows.a: An old friend needs a soft loan
rows.b: He needs ₦300,000 before Friday. He is not a bad person. He is also not employed right now, and you have heard this story before from other people.
It is 11pm. Three men with a torch and a vehicle that is not going anywhere until something changes hands.
Your younger sibling's school has sent the third reminder. The amount is not enormous. The expectation that you will handle it is.

rows.a: Estate levy and the community association
rows.b: The residents association has "resolved" that every household contributes to a new project. The chairman is standing in your compound with a receipt book.
Three weeks of tiredness that sleep does not fix. You can book a full check-up for ₦180,000, or assume it is stress and keep moving.
You have been running at this pace for a while. Something has to give and you get to choose what.

rows.a: Your phone left with someone else
rows.b: Danfo window seat, earphones in, and then it was gone. Everything is on that phone.
A partner at a firm you admire asks you to join a small working group. It meets on Saturdays for a year. The pay is nothing. The room is everything.

rows.a: A weekend contract lands in your lap
rows.b: Someone needs work done urgently and is willing to pay cash for a two-week sprint. It will eat every evening you have.
Your place of worship is building something. The pledge card has suggested amounts and everyone watches who fills what.
A man needs to exit a property fast — relocation, deadline, no time to negotiate. He is asking 60% of what comparable units went for last quarter.

rows.a: A letter with a government letterhead
rows.b: It is polite, numbered, and refers to "outstanding obligations". Someone has been filing things about you, or not filing things about you.

rows.a: A cousin is coming to stay
rows.b: He needs a place for "a few weeks" while he looks for work. Your flat has one room and he has already told the family you agreed.
An old account. A dormant balance. A refund nobody chased. ₦640,000 has your name on it.

rows.a: An industry event you were invited to
rows.b: A conference. The ticket is not cheap, the speakers are mid, but the hallway is where the actual value is.

rows.a: The car makes a new sound
rows.b: A sound that was not there last week. The mechanic says two words you did not want to hear: "gearbox" and "soon".

rows.a: Men have appeared on your land
rows.b: They have documents. You have documents. Both sets of documents cannot be right, and they have brought a surveyor who agrees with them.

more.name: More events — business, career, health, money

rows.b: ()=>'You delivered '+fmt(Math.round(S.biz.recv*0.4))+' of goods six weeks ago. The goods were accepted. The phone is now going to voicemail, and the person who signed for it has "travelled".'

A former employee, or someone who studied you closely, has launched a near-identical product at two-thirds of your price. They have copied the name, the packaging and, you notice, a typo from your own artwork.

()=>'Your landlord has decided to sell the building. You have first refusal on your own premises for '+fmt(Math.round(Math.max(12000000,(S.biz.capex\|\|0)*3)*S.cumInfl))+', or you can find somewhere else, or you can take your chances with whoever buys it.'

National power has been down for eleven days. Your generator is running nine hours a day, diesel has gone up 40%, and the generator itself has started making a noise that a mechanic has described, at length, as expensive.

rows.a: Half the team is thinking about leaving the country
rows.b: Two of your people have asked for references for visa applications. This is not about you. It is about the fact that everyone they know under thirty has a folder of documents and a plan.

rows.a: Your staff are running a business out of your business
rows.b: They are using your premises, your supplier account and, on two occasions you can prove, your stock. It is small. It is also systematic, and it has been going on for a while.

rows.a: A bad review is doing numbers
rows.b: One unhappy customer has written a long, specific, well-argued complaint and posted it where your customers will see it. Some of what they say is fair. Some of it is not. All of it is being shared.

rows.a: A new certification is now mandatory
rows.b: ()=>'A regulator has announced that from next quarter your category requires certification. The course and the inspection together cost about '+fmt(Math.round(900000*S.cumInfl))+'. Operating without it carries a fine of twice that, per quarter, once they start enforcing.'

rows.a: A bulk price, this week only
rows.b: Your supplier will sell you six months of input at 28% off if you pay today. That is a real discount and it is also all of your cash, in a warehouse, for two quarters.

rows.a: A relative would like a job
rows.b: A cousin has finished their degree and needs somewhere to start. Your mother has mentioned it twice. There is a real vacancy, and there are also better candidates.

()=>'A lender is offering '+fmt(Math.round(Math.max(3000000,(S.biz.revenue\|\|0)*0.5)))+' against your card receipts, approved in ten minutes, no paperwork. The rate is 7% a month. They are very clear about it and very cheerful.'

()=>'The local traders\' association has levied every business on the street for "security and sanitation". '+fmt(Math.round(250000*S.cumInfl))+'. Nobody can tell you what it buys. Everybody is paying.'

rows.a: Somebody abroad wants to franchise you
rows.b: A diaspora buyer has offered to open your brand in another country. They will pay a fee for the name and the system, and then operate it themselves. If it works, it is free money. If it fails, it is your name on a failing shop three thousand miles away.
()=>'A relative has been arrested and the family has called you, because you are the one they call. It is '+fmt(Math.round(700000*S.cumInfl))+' and it is needed tonight.'

rows.a: They would like to give you a title
rows.b: ()=>'Your community has decided you should take a chieftaincy title. It is an honour, it comes with obligations, and the committee has been very direct about the expected contribution of '+fmt(Math.round(3500000*S.cumInfl))+'.'
()=>'Somebody you grew up with has died, suddenly, at forty-one. There is a burial committee, a levy of '+fmt(Math.round(180000*S.cumInfl))+', and a widow with two children and no income.'

rows.a: Two years of rent, in advance
rows.b: ()=>'Your landlord will not renew annually any more. Two years, paid up front: '+fmt(Math.round(S.fin.budget.housing*24))+'. This is now common and it is not negotiable, only payable or not.'

rows.a: Something showed up on a scan
rows.b: A routine check has found something that needs a better scan and a specialist. It is probably nothing. "Probably" is doing a lot of work in that sentence.

rows.a: An old friend is now extremely successful
rows.b: Somebody you shared a room with in your twenties now runs something large. They have called, out of nowhere, to ask what you are doing with your life, and then to offer you a role that would pay roughly double.
Your community wants you to run for local office. It is unpaid, it will consume a year, and it is also the fastest way to become the person who is consulted about everything.

()=>'A distant relative has died and left you '+fmt(Math.round(4500000*S.cumInfl))+'. Two other people are disputing the will, and one of them has already changed the locks on a house that is not theirs.'
()=>'The school has sent the invoice and a reminder, and a note that places are confirmed on payment. '+fmt(Math.round(Math.max(600000, 400000*S.p.kids)*S.cumInfl))+'.'

()=>'A bank has written to say you are pre-approved for '+fmt(Math.round(Math.max(3000000, (salaryMonthly()+informalMonthly())*14)))+' at "just" 4.5% a month, with no collateral. The letter is friendly. The arithmetic is not.'

rows.a: There is a gap in the rate
rows.b: The official rate and the street rate have separated by 22%. For about a week, somebody with cash and the right contacts can move money through the gap. Everybody you know is doing it.
An insurance agent has asked a question you have been avoiding: if you died this year, what would your family actually live on? The honest answer appears to be "the sale of things, slowly".

rows.a: A pension scheme you have never read
rows.b: Your employer runs a contributory pension. You have been in it for years without looking at it. The statement shows a number, and the number is smaller than you expected, and the fund is invested mostly in government bonds.

rows.a: Everyone you know is buying the same thing
rows.b: It might be land in a particular corridor, a crypto token, a friend's startup, or imported cars. Whatever it is, everyone is making money and the people making money are telling everyone else about it.

policy.name: Policy events — the country does something to everyone

rows.b: Pump price triples before dawn. Transport, food and diesel repriced by lunchtime.

rows.a: Currency devalued at the official window
rows.b: The central bank unification lands. Importers reprice everything within a week.
New notes, no notes. POS operators become the most powerful people in the country for six weeks.
Borrowing gets expensive. Fixed income suddenly pays; equities and property stop moving.

rows.a: Central bank begins an easing cycle
rows.b: Credit loosens. Cheap money returns and risk assets breathe again.
The budget gaps widen, the currency wobbles, and government contracts stop paying.
Capital floods in. Valuations, land prices and confidence move together.
Eleven days of darkness. Diesel sellers and solar installers have a very good quarter.
A new independent grid deal lands. Businesses quietly stop budgeting for diesel.
Withholding, VAT and levies get restructured. Compliance costs go up for everyone formal.
Lenders must raise capital. Credit to small business dries up for two quarters.
A high-profile incident dominates the news. Logistics routes lengthen, insurance rises.

rows.a: A corporate client wants a large order
rows.b: The volume is three times your normal quarter. They want it delivered in six weeks and they want 90-day payment terms.
A customer posted a video. It has 400,000 views by Tuesday and your phone has not stopped since.
Your best person has been taking calls during lunch. A competitor is offering 40% more, and they have told you about it, which means they have not decided yet.

rows.a: The numbers do not add up
rows.b: Stock is disappearing. It is small enough to be invisible per day and large enough to matter per quarter. Someone in this building is taking it.
Two men, one clipboard, and a laminated ID each. They would like to see your registration documents, your tax clearance, and your fire certificate.
A 65% increase, effective next quarter. He knows exactly what it would cost you to move.

rows.a: A surge took out your equipment
rows.b: The grid came back on at 2am with enthusiasm. Some of your equipment did not come back with it.
Same product, cheaper, and they copied your branding closely enough that customers are asking if you are related.
Real money, published criteria, and a process. It will take three weeks of your life to prepare the bid.
They have seen the numbers and they would like to invest. The term sheet involves a valuation, a board seat, and a growth plan you will be held to.
They have elected a spokesperson. The ask is a 20% increase, and the timing is not an accident — it is your best quarter yet.
A genuine offer of credit — with a 4% premium baked into the price if you take it. You did not ask for the premium; it is simply in there.

rows.a: Your inputs are priced in dollars
rows.b: A devaluation lands mid-quarter. Your suppliers reprice before your customers will accept a new price. For six weeks, your margin simply does not exist.
Twenty-eight customers have complained in four days. The problem is traceable to one supplier batch and everyone can see it.

rows.b: function(){    const b=S.biz, d=angriestDirector(b); if(!d) return 'Somebody on your board has had enough.';    const A=archOf(d.arc);    return d.name+' has asked for a private word, which is how these things start. They have been on the board of '+b.name+      ' for '+Math.max(1, S.turn-(d.since\|\|S.turn))+' quarters, they have watched '+((b.profit\|\|0)>=0?'a business that works':'a business that does not')+      ', and they have come to the view that their name is attached to something they cannot influence. '+      '"I would rather go now, cleanly," they say, "than be in the room when it goes wrong." '+      'Patience '+Math.round(d.patience\|\|50)+'/100. Loyalty '+Math.round(d.loyalty\|\|50)+'/100. '+esc(A.blurb)+'.';  }

rows.a: function(){ const h=biggestHolder(S.biz); return h ? (h.name+' is selling their stake') : 'A shareholder is selling'; }
rows.b: function(){    const b=S.biz, h=biggestHolder(b); if(!h) return 'One of your shareholders is selling.';    const price=Math.round(bizValue(b)*((h.pct\|\|0)/100)*R.range(0.72,1.15));    S._gevPrice=price; S._gevHolder=h.id;    return h.name+' holds '+pct((h.pct\|\|0)/100,1)+' of '+b.name+' and has found a buyer \u2014 '+      R.pick(['a fund that specialises in distressed consumer businesses','a competitor you have lost tenders to',              'an overseas group buying into the sector','a consortium with no operating experience and a lot of money'])+      '. The price agreed is '+fmt(price)+'. Under the shareholders\u2019 agreement you '+      (deedOf(b).preEmption ? 'have a right of first refusal: you can buy it at that price before it transfers.'                             : 'have no pre-emption right. It can transfer without your consent.')+      (deedOf(b).tag ? ' You also have tag-along rights, which let you sell alongside on identical terms.' : '');  }

rows.a: function(){ const h=biggestHolder(S.biz); return h ? (h.name+' wants the company to buy from them') : 'A related-party proposal'; }
rows.b: function(){    const b=S.biz, h=biggestHolder(b); if(!h) return 'A shareholder wants to sell to the company.';    const amt=Math.round((b.revenue\|\|0)*R.range(0.10,0.26));    S._gevRel=amt; S._gevHolder=h.id;    return h.name+' owns another company. It supplies '+R.pick(['packaging','logistics','raw input','IT services','cleaning and facilities'])+      ', and it would like '+b.name+'\u2019s business: about '+fmt(amt)+' a year, on a three-year term. '+      'Their price is roughly '+R.int(8,26)+'% above what you pay now, which they describe as "certainty of supply". '+      'The board will have to approve it as a related-party transaction, and it will be minuted.';  }

function(){    const b=S.biz;    const d=boardOf(b).find(function(x){ return x.arc==='nominee'; });    S._gevDir=d?d.id:null;    const amt=Math.round((b.revenue\|\|0)*R.range(0.01,0.035)+400000*S.cumInfl);    S._gevFee=amt;    return (d?d.name:'Your government nominee')+' has mentioned, twice, that your '+R.pick(['operating licence','import permit','environmental clearance','sector registration'])+      ' is due for renewal, and that renewal "can be assisted". The figure discussed is '+fmt(amt)+      '. It would be invoiced as consultancy. Everyone in the room understands what it is, and nobody will write down that they said so.';  }

function(){    const b=S.biz;    return 'A holder of '+pct((b.externalPct\|\|0)/100,0)+' of '+b.name+' has filed a derivative action. '+      'The claim is that related-party contracts were approved without disclosure, that the company paid above market for them, '+      'and that you, as the controlling shareholder, caused it. They want the contracts set aside, an account of profits, and your removal as a director. '+      'They have counsel. Whether they win depends partly on the facts and partly on whether you wrote anything down.';  }

rows.a: function(){ return ((S.biz&&S.biz.md&&S.biz.md.name)\|\|'Your managing director')+' has been approached'; }
rows.b: function(){    const b=S.biz, m=b.md; if(!m) return 'Your managing director has been approached.';    const offer=Math.round(m.salary*R.range(1.7,2.6));    S._gevOffer=offer;    return m.name+' has been running '+b.name+' for '+Math.max(1,S.turn-(m.since\|\|S.turn))+' quarters. '+      'Somebody has offered them '+fmt(offer)+' a quarter \u2014 roughly '+Math.round(offer/Math.max(1,m.salary)*10)/10+      ' times what you pay \u2014 to run a larger operation. They have told you before accepting, which is either loyalty or leverage, '+      'and you have about a week to decide which it is.';  }

rows.a: The investors want their own managing director
rows.b: function(){    const b=S.biz;    return 'The holders of '+pct((b.externalPct\|\|0)/100,0)+' of '+b.name+' have written to you. They are, they say, delighted with progress. '+      'They also think the company has reached the size where it needs "professional management", which is the phrase used '+      'immediately before a founder is asked to become chairman. They have a candidate: '+      R.pick(['a former group MD of a listed company','an operator from a business three times this size','somebody who has done two turnarounds and one collapse'])+      ', at about '+fmt(Math.round(1100000*S.cumInfl))+' a quarter. They would like your view, by which they mean your agreement.';  }

function(){    const b=S.biz;    return 'It has happened three times now: a resolution split exactly down the middle, with the chair '+      (chairIsYours(b)?'using a casting vote to break it':'unable to break it, because the chair is not yours')+      '. The company is not being mismanaged so much as not being managed. Under the shareholders\u2019 agreement, deadlock is '+      (({mediation:'resolved by mediation', shotgun:'resolved by a shotgun clause', expert:'referred to an independent expert'})[deedOf(b).deadlock]\|\|'unresolved')+      ', and somebody on the other side has started quoting that clause at you.';  }

rows.a: function(){ const h=biggestHolder(S.biz); return h ? (h.name+' needs their money back') : 'A shareholder needs liquidity'; }
rows.b: function(){    const b=S.biz, h=biggestHolder(b); if(!h) return 'A shareholder needs their money back.';    const v=Math.max(1000000,bizValue(b));    const ask=Math.round(v*((h.pct\|\|0)/100)*R.range(0.55,0.85));    S._gevAsk=ask; S._gevHolder=h.id;    return h.name+' has called about something else entirely and got round to it in the last minute. '+      'They need liquidity \u2014 '+R.pick(['a property completion','a margin call','a divorce','a business of their own that is short'])+      ' \u2014 and they would rather sell to you than to a stranger. They are asking '+fmt(ask)+' for their '+      pct((h.pct\|\|0)/100,1)+', which is '+Math.round(ask/Math.max(1, v*((h.pct\|\|0)/100))*100)+'% of what the stake is worth on paper. Math.round(v)+'%' : v.toFixed(2)+'x'); };    return 'The certificate is due under the facility from '+x.c.from+'. '+esc(K.desc)+' '+      'The limit is '+fmtv(x.c.limit)+'. You are at '+fmtv(x.actual)+'. '+      (x.c.kind==='leverage' ? 'Trailing EBITDA is '+fmt(a.ebitda)+' against borrowings of '+fmt(a.debt)+'.'       : x.c.kind==='cover' ? 'Trailing EBITDA is '+fmt(a.ebitda)+' and the annual interest bill is '+fmt(a.interest*4)+'.'       : x.c.kind==='mincash' ? 'The company closed the quarter with '+fmt(a.closeCash)+'.'       : x.c.kind==='capex' ? 'Trailing capital spend is '+fmt(b.capex12\|\|0)+'.'       : x.c.kind==='conc' ? 'One customer is '+Math.round(x.actual)+'% of revenue.'       : 'You are no longer the managing director, which is an event of default under the facility.')+      ' This is not the end of the company. careers.label: Work late, deliver hard
careers.note: Four extra hours a week, every week, for a whole quarter. It works, and then it stops working. The second lot of late nights in one quarter buys far less than the first.

careers.label: Take people to lunch
careers.note: Relationship capital compounds faster than money capital early on. It takes afternoons, though, and the same people can only be asked to lunch so often before it becomes a story about you.

careers.label: Ask for a raise
careers.note: Odds scale with performance, tenure and how replaceable you are.

careers.label: Interview elsewhere
careers.note: The fastest way to close the gap between what you are paid and what you are worth.

careers.label: Run a side hustle after hours
careers.note: Seven hours a week of evenings and weekends, sold off in blocks. There are only so many nights in a quarter — take on a second hustle and the second one comes out of your sleep.

careers.label: Resign and go full-time on the business
careers.note: Burn the boats. Business output jumps — and so does the cost of being wrong.

careers.label: Take a month off to reset
careers.note: Sometimes the highest-return action available is stopping. Once a year, at most — a month off every quarter is not a sabbatical, it is unemployment.

goods.label: Laptop
goods.note: A tool, not a toy. Doubles as your office.

goods.label: Generator (big boy)
goods.note: The single most Nigerian purchase in existence. Fuel not included.

goods.label: Solar + Inverter
goods.note: Capital now, silence forever. Pays back in ~4 years.

goods.label: Used Car
goods.note: Freedom, status, and a maintenance schedule that never ends.

goods.label: Furnish the flat
goods.note: You stop feeling like you are camping.

goods.label: Proper Wardrobe
goods.note: People absolutely do judge. Especially in this town.

goods.label: Health Insurance
goods.note: Turns a catastrophic event into an annoying one.

goods.label: Professional Certification
goods.note: ACA, CFA, PMP. Signals competence to strangers.

goods.label: Executive MBA
goods.note: Buying a network with a diploma attached.

assets.label: Bank Savings
assets.note: Instant access. Loses to inflation, every single quarter.

assets.label: Ajo / Esusu Group
assets.note: Informal rotating savings. Decent return, real risk the collector disappears.

assets.label: Treasury Bills
assets.note: Sovereign short-term. Priced off the central bank rate.

assets.label: Fixed Deposit
assets.note: Locked 90 days. Break it and you lose the interest.

assets.label: Government Bonds
assets.note: Long duration. Price falls when rates rise.

assets.label: Local Equities
assets.note: The domestic stock market. Violent drawdowns, violent recoveries.

assets.label: Dollar Account
assets.note: Pure FX hedge. Earns nothing, protects everything.

assets.label: Global Equity ETF
assets.note: Broad index in hard currency. Your returns are amplified by devaluation.

assets.label: REIT / Property Fund
assets.note: Listed real estate. Liquid-ish, moves with rates and rent.

assets.label: Land (peri-urban)
assets.note: Illiquid, title risk is real, but this is where generational money is made.

assets.label: Rental Property
assets.note: Completed unit. Rents come in, tenants happen.

assets.label: Gold
assets.note: Crisis hedge. Boring until the quarter it is not.

assets.label: Crypto
assets.note: Genuinely life-changing and genuinely ruinous. Position size is the only real skill.

deals.label: Property flip
deals.note: A unit that needs work and a seller who needs to be somewhere else. Four quarters to turn it.

deals.label: Private placement
deals.note: A growing company wants money before it wants a valuation. Illiquid for at least two years.

deals.label: Distressed stock
deals.note: A business is closing. Stock, equipment and a customer list, priced to move this week.

deals.label: Bridge loan
deals.note: Ninety days, twelve per cent, secured against a contract that has already been signed. Everyone says it is safe.

deals.label: Import arbitrage
deals.note: Buy here, sell there, before the next FX move. The window is about one quarter wide.

deals.label: Land banking
deals.note: A corridor nobody wants yet. Nothing happens for two years and then everything happens.

deals.label: Franchise unit
deals.note: A proven brand wants an operator with capital. You supply both and follow their system.

deals.label: Equipment purchase
deals.note: Buy the machine your business keeps renting. It pays for itself or it sits in the yard.

covenants.label: Leverage
covenants.note: Borrowings must stay below a multiple of trailing EBITDA.

covenants.label: Interest cover
covenants.note: Trailing EBITDA must cover interest a set number of times.

covenants.label: Minimum cash
covenants.note: The company must hold at least this much cash at every quarter end.

covenants.label: Capital expenditure cap
covenants.note: Capital spend in any four quarters may not exceed this.

covenants.label: Customer concentration
covenants.note: No single customer may exceed this share of revenue.

covenants.label: Key person
covenants.note: The founder must remain managing director, or the facility falls for review.

resolutions.label: Fund the company or be diluted

household.label: Housekeeper
household.note: The house stops being a second job. Nothing dramatic, every single week.

household.label: Cook
household.note: You eat properly and at the same hour. It turns up in your bloodwork a decade later.

household.label: Nanny
household.note: Childcare that is not you at two in the morning. The largest single block of attention you can buy.

household.label: Driver
household.note: Traffic stops being your job. You arrive composed and you work in the back seat.

household.label: Gardener
household.note: Grounds, generator, gutters. Property upkeep falls and the place looks like somebody owns it.

household.label: Security
household.note: A gate and a man on it. Cuts theft at home and, if you post him there, at the business.

household.label: Personal assistant
household.note: Your calendar, your calls, the birthday you always forget. The best return on attention on this list.

household.label: Chief of staff
household.note: Runs your affairs across every company you own. Partly covers businesses that have no general manager.

household.label: Accountant
household.note: Books kept properly across the companies and your own affairs. Tax exposure falls, compliance rises.

household.label: Lawyer
household.note: Reads what you are about to sign. Contracts tighten and disputes cost less when they arrive.

perks.label: Accommodation
perks.note: They live in. Cheaper than the equivalent allowance, and they are always there.

perks.label: Transport
perks.note: You cover getting to work and back.

perks.label: Feeding
perks.note: One proper meal a day on you.

perks.label: Medical
perks.note: A retainer at a clinic. They stop bringing you their problems.

perks.label: 13th month
perks.note: An extra month every December. The cheapest way to keep somebody through a hard year.

negotiation.label: Anchor hard
negotiation.note: Name a number near your best case and defend it. Moves them a long way when it works.

negotiation.label: Argue it with numbers
negotiation.note: Comparables, margins, what the market actually pays. Effective and low-risk if your finance skill is real.

negotiation.label: Make a genuine concession
negotiation.note: Move meaningfully to unlock movement from them. Costs you, nearly always closes.

negotiation.label: Hold firm and say nothing
negotiation.note: Free. Works when they are under time pressure and badly when they are not.

negotiation.label: Trade a term instead of price
negotiation.note: Give something that costs you less than cash: notice period, payment days, exclusivity, a title.

negotiation.label: Use your leverage
negotiation.note: Remind them, concretely, what you bring and what it costs them to lose you. You can only spend this once.

negotiation.label: Walk away
negotiation.note: Ends it. Sometimes the only leverage you ever actually had.

staff.label: Finance
staff.note: Improves the books and reduces tax risk.

staff.label: General manager
staff.note: Runs the unit without you. Frees your attention for other companies.

levers.label: Second shift
levers.gives: Capacity +35% for as long as it runs.
levers.ask: Run the units a second time

levers.label: Input supply contract
levers.gives: Cost of goods about 10% lower for the term.

levers.label: Distribution deal
levers.ask: Hand the selling to a distributor

traits.label: Sharp
traits.note: High output, negotiates hard on salary.

traits.label: Connected
traits.note: Brings clients and shortcuts with them.

traits.label: Light fingers
traits.note: Inventory goes missing. You will find out late.

traits.label: Ambitious
traits.note: Grows fast, leaves faster if underpaid.

traits.label: Genuinely excellent
traits.note: Top decile. You will struggle to keep them.

ambitions.label: Clean millionaire by 40
ambitions.note: Net worth of ₦500m in start-of-game money before you turn forty, with no debt hanging off it.

ambitions.label: Build something that outlasts you
ambitions.note: Raise a family, keep them close, and leave behind more than money.

ambitions.label: Never need anyone again
ambitions.note: A Freedom Index above 80 with zero debt. Work becomes a choice.

ambitions.label: Build the biggest thing you can
ambitions.note: Scale a business past ₦250m of quarterly revenue and employ more than twenty people.

ambitions.label: Buy back what was lost
ambitions.note: Own land and property worth ₦1bn in start-of-game money. The family gets the point.

eras.label: Ordinary Times
eras.head: Nothing is happening, which is its own kind of luck.

eras.label: The Boom
eras.head: Money is cheap, valuations are silly, and everyone you know is suddenly an investor.

eras.label: The Bust
eras.head: The music stopped. Nobody wants to admit they were still dancing.

eras.label: The Long Stagnation
eras.head: Nothing collapses. Nothing improves. Years go by like this.

eras.label: Reform Season
eras.head: New rules, new taxes, new forms. Some of this is good for you. Most of it is paperwork.

eras.label: Election Season
eras.head: Promises are cheap, contracts are frozen, and everyone with a file is waiting for the result.

eras.label: Crisis
eras.head: Something broke. Nobody agrees what, and the argument is expensive.

seasonAxes.label: Wealth
seasonAxes.why: What you are worth in real terms, after inflation has had its say.

seasonAxes.label: Enterprise
seasonAxes.why: Not what a business earned, but that you built one that would still be standing without you.

seasonAxes.label: Reputation
seasonAxes.why: What your name is worth in a room you are not in.

seasonAxes.label: Family
seasonAxes.why: Who is actually there at the end of it.

seasonAxes.label: Health
seasonAxes.why: You have to be alive and well enough to enjoy any of the rest of this.

seasonAxes.label: Integrity
seasonAxes.why: Whether you got there in a way you could describe out loud.

board.label: Founder
board.note: you, in the chair, holding the casting vote

board.label: Capital
board.note: counts the quarters since the last distribution

board.label: Operations
board.note: thinks the answer to most questions is more capacity

board.label: Access
board.note: knows who to call, and expects to be credited for it

board.label: Craft
board.note: cares whether the thing actually works

board.label: Family
board.note: represents a surname, not a shareholding

board.label: Non-executive
board.note: reads the numbers before the narrative

board.label: Strategic
board.note: bought in intending to end up with all of it

board.label: Government nominee
board.note: speaks for a ministry that holds opinions about your sector

profiles.label: The Fresh Graduate
profiles.note: Degree fresh, account empty. You have time, energy and zero leverage.

profiles.label: The Corporate Climber
profiles.note: Good salary, better title, and a lifestyle that quietly eats all of it.

profiles.label: The Relentless Founder
profiles.note: You left school to build. High hustle, low runway, no safety net.

profiles.label: The Market Trader
profiles.note: Cash moves through your hands daily. Informal, fast, and completely undocumented.

profiles.label: The Returnee
profiles.note: Came back with savings, a foreign degree, and a family that now expects miracles.

endings.condition: You reach 65, or turn 168 (42 years). The run closes on its own terms.
The season finish line you joined, or set, arrives. It takes precedence over every other ending.
Cash is deeply negative, debts exceed ₦1m and credit is under 22. On Hardcore the run ends here; below it, assets are seized and you continue with less.
Health reaches zero. Nothing buys it back at that point.

repercussions: A decision can schedule its own bill: `{turn, title, text, eff}`. It arrives as a modal, on the quarter it comes due.
Assets are seized against the debt, credit collapses to 14, stress +18, happiness −14, reputation −10. You continue with less.
Interest and repayments are drawn every quarter; credit score gates what you can borrow next.
Cash loses purchasing power every quarter. The currency can also devalue, which hurts imports and helps exporters.
Leverage, cover, distributions, capex, liquidity and owner drawings. Breach is recorded and priced.
A breach in one group company can pull the others in.
Directors have tempers and patience; resolutions pass or fail on votes, and the register records both.
A competitor undercuts, poaches or expands; ignoring it has a cost.
Friends, siblings, parents and partners age, ask for money, get ill and die.
High stress erodes health and happiness; low happiness bleeds into output.
Without capacity, staff, price or demand, revenue falls and upkeep still lands.
Committed capital is at risk: the deal wins or loses, on the odds you were shown.
Above ₦3m revenue, somebody asks for a stake. Accepting changes who owns the business.
Stories have stages; a stage not answered comes back on its own schedule.
